# Best AI for ACORD form filling (2026): 7 tools compared


Abhi Balijepalli


Co-founder, CopyCat


Published November 16, 2026


·


9 min read


Quick picks


- **Best overall for commercial agencies:**[CopyCat ACORD Submissions](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-form-automation) . Fills every ACORD in the submission from the documents you already have, cites every value, flags gaps and lets you edit on the form.
- **Best if you also want carrier portals keyed for you:** Cooper.
- **Best for one-off PDF filling:** Instafill.ai.
- **Best when the client should fill out the application:** Broker Buddha, or Indio for Applied Epic agencies.
- **Best budget intake-to-ACORD for small agencies:** InsurGrid.


"AI that fills ACORD forms" now covers very different products. Some read the account's documents and fill the whole submission. Some fill one PDF at a time from data you paste in. Some send the client a questionnaire and turn the answers into ACORDs. This guide sorts seven of them by the job they do, so you can shortlist two and test them on a real account.


We make CopyCat, so our first pick is not independent. Every other tool is described from its vendor's public materials as of November 2026. Check current details with each vendor.


## How we judged


A filled ACORD is only useful if an account manager can trust it without retyping it. That comes down to five questions:


Question Why it matters


Does it read what you already have? Prior ACORDs, dec pages, loss runs, MVRs and schedules hold most of the answers. A tool that needs the data re-entered saves little.


Does it show where each value came from? A page citation turns checking a FEIN or a VIN into one click instead of a search.


Does it flag gaps instead of guessing? A blank marked for review is safe. A plausible guess on a year built or a loss is an E&O problem.


Can you edit on the form? Corrections should happen on the ACORD itself, not in a side panel you then re-export.


Does one read fill every form? The insured, locations and drivers repeat across the 125, 126, 127 and 140. They should be entered once.

## 1. CopyCat ACORD Submissions: best overall for commercial agencies


Best for: commercial account managers who build submissions from a pile of documents. You drop in last year's ACORDs and carrier apps, dec pages, loss runs, MVRs, vehicle spreadsheets and SOVs, pick the lines of business, and CopyCat fills the[ACORD 125](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-125) , the line sections and the schedules from one read. Each fact carries a citation to its page, anything the documents don't answer is flagged instead of guessed, and the forms open in an editor where you click any field to change it or ask the assistant ("FEIN is 84-2291736, add umbrella") to update every form at once.


Download all hands over every finished PDF plus a marketing summary workbook, and Email summary drafts the submission email to the carriers in your market list that write those lines. CopyCat is a member of ACORD and fills current editions, such as the ACORD 125 and 126 (2025/03) and ACORD 130 (2026/08). It sits in the same workspace as CopyCat's quote comparisons and proposals, so the quotes that come back go straight into the client proposal.


## 2. Cooper: best if you also want carrier portals keyed


Best for: agencies that want the same risk entered into carrier portals. Cooper reads dec pages, loss runs and applications from email or a connected AMS, fills the ACORD forms and carrier supplements, and flags what is missing. Its distinct feature is carrier portal entry. Pricing is not public.


## 3. Instafill.ai: best for one-off PDF filling


Best for: filling individual fillable PDFs, including ACORD 25 certificates and the 125, 126, 127 and 140. It is a general AI PDF filler with an insurance page: you upload a form and your data and it completes the fields. It is not built around a submission workflow or your market list. Self-service starts at $99 a month for 50 documents. Some of its form pages cover older editions, so confirm the edition before you send.


## 4. Broker Buddha: best when the client fills out the application


Best for: agencies that want the insured to answer an online questionnaire instead of a PDF. Broker Buddha turns carrier and ACORD applications into smart forms, shows the client last year's values on renewal, turns the answers into ACORD forms and Excel workbooks, and captures an e-signature. It depends on the client finishing the form. Broker Buddha Lite starts at $99 a month.


## 5. Indio: best for Applied Epic agencies sending digital applications


Best for: Applied Epic agencies. Indio, from Applied Systems, sends clients digital applications from a large library of carrier and ACORD forms and exchanges account and ACORD data with Epic in both directions. Like Broker Buddha, it is client-completed rather than read from documents.


## 6. InsurGrid: best budget intake-to-ACORD for small agencies


Best for: small agencies collecting new-business data. InsurGrid sends one intake link; the client answers questions, connects a carrier or uploads documents, and an AI generator maps the result into editable ACORD 125, 126, 130, 140, 80 and 185 PDFs for the agent to finish. It launched in July 2026 and is included in the $99 a month plan.


## 7. Coverflow: worth a look if you already use it


Coverflow's Fill ACORD Form feature drafts ACORD forms from uploaded documents. Its help center lists several common commercial forms, including the 127, 131, 140 and 160, as coming soon, so check the current form list against what your agency sends.


## Filling is not the same as extracting


If you search for "AI ACORD" you will also find FurtherAI, Docsumo, Nomad Data and similar tools. They read data out of ACORD forms that arrive, which is what carriers, MGAs and wholesalers need. An agency needs the opposite: blank forms filled from the account's documents. Pick from the right category.


## Run a 30-minute bake-off


1. **Pick your messiest real account.** Scanned dec pages, a loss run, an MVR, a vehicle spreadsheet and last year's application.
2. **Run it through two tools.** Same documents, same lines of business.
3. **Check ten hard fields.** FEIN, class codes, five years of losses, three VINs, year built and square footage.
4. **Count the lookups.** How many values did you have to find yourself, and did the tool show its source or guess?
5. **Send the result.** Would you put your name on the PDF without retyping it? That is the test that matters.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best AI for ACORD form filling?


For commercial agencies filling from the documents they already have, CopyCat ACORD Submissions. Cooper fits agencies that also want carrier portals keyed, Instafill.ai fits one-off PDFs, and Broker Buddha or Indio fit client-completed applications.


### Can ChatGPT or Claude fill out ACORD forms?


A general assistant can read and summarize documents, but it does not reliably write values into the hundreds of fillable fields on a current ACORD PDF, keep facts consistent across forms, or show the page each value came from.


### Which ACORD forms can AI fill?
